summary: Keep host-test source fixtures outside recursive runtime state

delivery.outcome: Keep host-test fixtures within the canonical repository cache and copy only canonical Subactor control files, preventing recursive copies of runtime state during governed source release checks.
nonGoals: No runtime/controller/publisher deployment or protected-policy changes in this source slice
No tag/Release, registry publish, target adoption or legacy metadata movement
No changes to production installer semantics, package projections or foreign worktrees

architecture.decision: The existing native host-test suite owns its private fixture cache. The broken-source fixture preserves canonical .subactor/manifest.json and .gitignore while excluding runtime state and its own nested cache; the actual integration exercise supplies the recursion regression.
architecture.rollback: Revert the reviewed material source change through protected publication; preserve runtime data and do not restore external scratch helpers.

validation.evidence: Native suite itself creates nested fixtures under owning repository cache. Assert canonical Subactor control files survive while runtime/cache paths are absent; no recursion and no copy of original legacy metadata.

commands: Independent exact-head protected CI and Validator
validation.evidence: Complete staged/committed scope gate, required hosted checks and protected independent review/merge. No self-approval or deployment.
